subsystems.name: Blood collection and cfDNA isolation
subsystems.role: obtains plasma and extracts the tiny fragments of cell-free DNA shed by tumours.

subsystems.name: Library preparation and sequencing
subsystems.role: converts cfDNA into sequenceable libraries and reads them at high depth.

subsystems.name: Methylation and genomic analysis
subsystems.role: identifies cancer-specific methylation patterns and other DNA features.

subsystems.name: Machine learning classifier
subsystems.role: distinguishes cancer signals from background and predicts the tissue of origin.

subsystems.name: Clinical reporting and follow-up
subsystems.role: returns results and directs patients to confirmatory tests.

buildSteps.title: Discover biomarkers
buildSteps.detail: Compare cfDNA from people with and without cancer to find methylation signatures and fragment patterns linked to tumours.

buildSteps.title: Build training datasets
buildSteps.detail: Collect thousands of blood samples with known cancer status, stage and type from diverse populations.

buildSteps.title: Train the classifier
buildSteps.detail: Use machine learning to recognise cancer signals and assign a likely tissue of origin.

buildSteps.title: Validate in case-control studies
buildSteps.detail: Test sensitivity and specificity in independent samples that were not used for training.

buildSteps.title: Run prospective screening trials
buildSteps.detail: Screen large numbers of asymptomatic people to measure real-world performance and whether cancers are found earlier.

buildSteps.title: Obtain regulatory review
buildSteps.detail: Submit evidence to regulators for approval as a screening test, which requires proof of clinical benefit.

buildSteps.title: Integrate into clinical care
buildSteps.detail: Establish pathways for positive results, including rapid imaging and biopsy, so that detected cancers are acted on promptly.

prerequisites.why: tumours shed DNA into the blood, and its methylation patterns differ from normal DNA.
reading millions of cfDNA fragments per sample is required to detect rare cancer signals.
classifiers need broad training data to work across ages, ancestries and cancer types.
demonstrated in research, but clinical validation and avoiding false positives remain challenging.
a positive blood test must be quickly confirmed with imaging or biopsy, which many health systems cannot yet guarantee.

pathway.milestone: commercial tests available by prescription, but not recommended for general population screening
pathway.unlocks: early adopters and research studies can use them, while evidence accumulates.

pathway.milestone: results from large prospective trials measuring stage shift and cancer-specific mortality
pathway.unlocks: proof that MCED actually saves lives, not just finds cancers.

pathway.milestone: regulatory approval and inclusion in national screening guidelines
pathway.unlocks: reimbursement and routine use in primary care.

pathway.milestone: integration with existing single-cancer screening and risk-based personalised programmes
pathway.unlocks: a shift from late diagnosis to population-wide early detection.
